SOAH DOCKET NO. 473-26-16349
PUC DOCKET NO. 59475

BEFORE THE STATE OFFICE OF ADMINISTRATIVE HEARINGS

INTERVENORS ALISON BECHTER (TRACT 3510) AND AARON C. BECHTER
(TRACT 3509)

MOTION TO ESTABLISH RESPONSE DEADLINE AND REQUEST FOR EXPEDITED
ORDER

REGARDING APPLICANTS' OBJECTIONS TO AND MOTION TO STRIKE
INTERVENOR TESTIMONY

TO THE HONORABLE ADMINISTRATIVE LAW JUDGES:

Intervenors Alison Bechter (Tract 3510, Interchange Item No. 4349) and Aaron C. Bechter
(Tract 3509), appearing pro se, respectfully file this Motion to Establish a Response Deadline
and Request for Expedited Order. This motion arises from the Objections to and Motion to Strike
Intervenor Testimony filed by Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC and LCRA Transmission
Services Corporation (collectively, "Applicants") in this proceeding.

I. BACKGROUND

On or about May 13, 2026, Applicants filed their Objections to and Motion to Strike Intervenor
Testimony, identifying over 700 pieces of intervenor testimony — spanning thousands of pages
— and moving to strike portions of those testimonies on grounds of hearsay, non-expert opinion,
and relevance. The motion is comprehensive in scope and affects a substantial number of pro se
intervenors who are individual landowners without legal representation in this proceeding.

Intervenors Alison Bechter and Aaron C. Bechter contacted PUC Docket Specialist and Attorney
Scott Miles on May 20, 2026 to inquire about the deadline for affected intervenors to file
responses to Applicants' Motion to Strike. Mr. Miles confirmed that, to his knowledge, no
response deadline has been established or identified by the Administrative Law Judges or any
party in connection with this motion. Mr. Miles has indicated he will contact the Administrative
Law Judges and counsel for Applicants regarding this issue.

Given the absence of a response deadline, and given the compressed 180-day statutory timeline
governing this proceeding, Intervenors respectfully request that the Administrative Law Judges
issue an expedited order establishing a clear deadline by which affected intervenors may file
responses to Applicants’ Motion to Strike.

II. GROUNDS FOR RELIEF


 1. No Response Deadline Has Been Established. Applicants' Motion to Strike was filed
pursuant to SOAH Order No. 6. However, SOAH Order No. 6 does not appear to have
established a corresponding deadline for intervenor responses to that motion. The absence
of a response deadline leaves affected intervenors — the vast majority of whom are pro
se landowners — without notice of when or whether they may be heard in opposition to a
motion that could strike portions of their filed testimony.

2. Due Process Requires an Opportunity to Respond. Applicants’ motion seeks to strike
testimony from hundreds of individual intervenors who have exercised their right to
participate in this proceeding as affected landowners. Basic principles of due process and
fair administrative procedure require that those intervenors be given a meaningful
opportunity to respond before any portion of their testimony is struck from the record. An

opportunity to respond is meaningless without a clear deadline by which responses must
be filed.

3. The Compressed Statutory Timeline Requires Expedited Handling. This proceeding
is governed by a 180-day statutory deadline running from the date of the CCN application
filing. Given the proximity of the hearing and the volume of testimony at issue, any delay
in establishing a response deadline risks prejudicing affected intervenors who cannot
prepare and file adequate responses without knowing when those responses are due.
Expedited handling of this procedural issue is warranted.

4. Pro Se Intervenors Require Clear Procedural Guidance. The overwhelming majority
of intervenors affected by Applicants' motion are individual landowners proceeding
without legal counsel. These intervenors may be unaware that a motion to strike has been
filed against their testimony, may not understand that they have a right to respond, and
cannot be expected to navigate the response process without clear deadlines and
procedural guidance from the ALJs. An expedited order establishing a response deadline,
and directing that notice of the deadline be provided to affected intervenors through the
PUCT Interchange, would serve the interests of fairness and orderly administration of
this proceeding.

5. Selective Application Raises Procedural Fairness Concerns Requiring Prompt
Resolution. As one specific example, Applicants’ motion targets the exhibit attachments
in the Direct Testimony of Alison Bechter (Interchange Item No. 4349) on hearsay
grounds. However, the Direct Testimony of Aaron C. Bechter (Tract 3509), filed in the
same docket on the same date, contains structurally identical exhibit attachments with
identical framing language — and is not identified anywhere in Applicants! Exhibit A.
This inconsistency is a concrete procedural fairness issue that Intervenors are prepared to
brief in a formal response, but can only do so if a response deadline is established and the
opportunity to be heard is provided.

Ill. REQUESTED RELIEF

Intervenors Alison Bechter and Aaron C. Bechter respectfully request that the Administrative
Law Judges issue an expedited order that:

 6, Establishes a specific date and time by which affected intervenors may file responses to
Applicants' Objections to and Motion to Strike Intervenor Testimony. Intervenors
respectfully suggest a response deadline of no earlier than June 5, 2026 at 5:00 p.m.
Central Time, or alternatively, no fewer than fourteen (14) calendar days from the date of
the ALJs' order establishing the deadline, whichever is later. This proposed deadline
reflects the volume and complexity of the motion, the number of affected pro se
intervenors, the likelihood that many affected intervenors are not yet aware the motion
was filed, and the time required for unrepresented landowners to prepare a meaningful
written response without legal counsel;

7. Directs that notice of the established response deadline be posted in the PUCT
Interchange under Docket No. $9475 and SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349 so that all
affected intervenors have access to that information;

8. Confirms that all affected intervenors — including pro se landowner intervenors —- have
the right to file a written response opposing Applicants’ motion before any ruling is
issued striking their testimony;

9. Provides that no testimony will be struck on the basis of Applicants’ motion until after the
established response deadline has passed and affected intervenors have had a meaningful
opportunity to be heard; and

10, Grants such other and further procedural relief as the Administrative Law Judges deem
appropriate to protect the due process rights of affected pro se intervenors in this
proceeding.

IV. CONCLUSION

Hundreds of individual Texas landowners have exercised their legal right to participate in this
proceeding and have filed direct testimony at significant personal effort and expense. They are
entitled to know that a motion has been filed to strike portions of their testimony, to know the
deadline by which they may respond, and to have a meaningful opportunity to be heard before
that testimony is struck. Intervenors Alison Bechter and Aaron C. Bechter respectfully urge the
Administrative Law Judges to issue an expedited order without delay establishing the procedural
framework that fairness and due process require.

Respectfully submitted,

Alison Bechter, Pro Se
Intervenor — Tract 3510

8564. Shaw Road, Rogers

Aaron C. Bechte

 Intervenor — Tract 3509
8564 Shaw Road, Rogers, Texas 76569

Date: May 20, 2026

CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE

I certify that a true and correct copy of this Motion has been served on all parties of record in
PUC Docket No. 59475 and SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349 in accordance with applicable

service requirements, including counsel for Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC and LCRA
Transmission Services Corporation.
